quickfire.question: The balance factor of an AVL node is defined as: height(_____ subtree) − height(right subtree)

routineWriter.questionText: Write the balanceFactor routine for an AVL tree node. Return the difference of left and right subtree heights. Handle NULL nodes.

commonMistakes.description: NULL node has balance factor 0 — omitting this causes null-dereference on the height call
Always left minus right — reversing the order gives wrong rotation direction

quickfire.question: The minimum number of nodes in an AVL tree of height h follows the recurrence N(h) = N(h-1) + N(h-2) + _____

routineWriter.questionText: The question bank asks: 'What is the minimum number of nodes in an AVL tree of height 15?' Use the recurrence N(h) = N(h-1) + N(h-2) + 1 with N(0)=1, N(1)=2. Compute N(15). Show the recurrence reasoning — you won't be expected to compute by hand beyond understanding the pattern.
routineWriter.scaffoldCode:
/* Show the recurrence pattern:
   N(0) = 1
   N(1) = 2
   N(2) = N(1) + N(0) + 1 = ?
   ...
   N(h) = N(h-1) + N(h-2) + 1
   Compute N(15) step by step */

commonMistakes.description: The +1 accounts for the root itself — forgetting it gives Fibonacci numbers, not AVL minimum nodes
Base cases: height-0 tree has 1 node (root only); height-1 tree has 2 nodes (root + one child)

quickfire.question: A right rotation on node Y promotes which node to become the new subtree root?

routineWriter.questionText: Write the rotateRight routine for an AVL tree. Y is the current subtree root, X is Y's left child.

commonMistakes.description: Save x->right before overwriting — it becomes y's new left child
x takes y's place as root, so y becomes x's right child
y's left must be T2 (x's old right subtree) — it was the only subtree that needs rehoming
Return the new root (x) so the parent can relink

quickfire.question: Inserting 1, 2, 3 into an empty AVL tree causes which rotation at node 1?

fullTrace.questionText: Show the step-by-step result of inserting 1, 3, 5, 7, 19, 17, 15, 13, 11, 9, 0 into an initially empty AVL tree (direct Part-B Q9 from the question bank).

steps.note: 3 > 1 → right of 1. Root BF = -1. Still balanced.
5 > 1, 5 > 3 → right of 3. Root BF = -2 (RR case). Left-rotate at 1. New root = 3 (1 left, 5 right).
7 > 3, 7 > 5 → right of 5. BF at 3 = -2 (RR case). Left-rotate at 3. New root = 5 (3 left, 7 right), 1 left of 3.
19 > 5, 19 > 7 → right of 7. BF at 5 = -2 (RR). Left-rotate at 5... cascades up. New structure: 7 root (5 left, 19 right); 5 has 3 left; 3 has 1 left.
17 goes between 7 and 19. BF at 19 = 1 (left-heavy). 7's right subtree: 17 left of 19. No rotation yet.
15 goes right of 17... RL case at 19. Right-rotate at 17 then left-rotate at 19. 17 becomes parent of 15 and 19.
13 < 17, 13 > 7... left of 17, right of 7? Trace carefully. No rotation if balanced.
Causes rebalancing — trace balance factors bottom-up to find first unbalanced ancestor.
Causes rebalancing — LL or LR case depending on position.
0 < 1 → leftmost insertion. May cause rebalancing up the left spine.
